title: Secret Santa
logline: Michael draws Toby in Secret Santa and can't trade him away, the Party Planning Committee splits into two rival parties, and Jim gives Pam a box of their inside jokes, keeping back the card that says why.
outline: A: Michael draws Toby for Secret Santa, fails to trade him, tries to merge two rival parties, and is undone by Toby's thoughtful gift. B: Jim drew Pam; his gift is a box of their inside jokes, and he pockets the card. C: The Party Planning Committee splits, Angela's silent party versus Kelly's karaoke, and Oscar notices Dwight and Angela drew each other. Order: cold, A, B, C, A, C, A, B, C, A, B, tag
theme: The gift that says too much
storySoFar: At Christmas, Michael drew Toby for Secret Santa and couldn't trade him; he gave Toby a 'Get Out of Jail Free' card, and Toby, who drew Michael, gave him an engraved pen: 'Michael Scott, Regional Manager, Scranton.' The Party Planning Committee split into Angela's quiet party and Kelly's karaoke until Michael merged them, with only quiet songs (Kevin sang a lovely Silent Night). Jim drew Pam and gave her a box of their inside jokes: a Twix, a beet, the Dundies umbrella, the cricket radio and a sketchbook 'for the children's books'; he pocketed the card and told her there wasn't one. Dwight and Angela drew each other (a carved cat, an engraved pocketknife); Oscar is 'keeping a file'. Kelly sang karaoke to Ryan, who stayed. Corporate decides at month's end whether Scranton or Stamford closes; Jim's Stamford transfer is pending; Pam's wedding is June 10.

stateChanges.progress: Jim's Christmas gift was a box of inside jokes; he kept the card that says how he feels
They drew each other for Secret Santa; Oscar caught them in the kitchen and is keeping a mental file
Ryan stayed for one more karaoke song with Kelly

stateChanges.status: Toby gave Michael a perfect gift; Michael still hates him, slightly less

stateChanges.text: Jim still has the unread Christmas card for Pam in his pocket
Toby's pen: 'Michael Scott, Regional Manager, Scranton'
Kevin has a surprisingly beautiful singing voice

scenes.recap: Michael hangs mistletoe in his doorway; the first person under it is Toby, and Michael flees.

beats.text: DECEMBER 22

beats.caption: tapes a sprig of mistletoe above his office door

lines: Mistletoe is a Christmas tradition that goes back to the Druids.
And Jan is coming by later. Maybe. To drop off a form. Under here.

beats.text: Michael, I just need you to sign the holiday party liability—
NO. Not under there. Get out from under there. That is not for you.

scenes.recap: The Secret Santa drawing: Michael draws Toby, and Angela announces there will be no trades.

beats.text: Secret Santa rules. Twenty-dollar limit. No trades. No exceptions. No gag gifts, Kevin.

beats.caption: pulls a slip from the bowl and reads it

beats.text: Is there a re-draw? For medical reasons?
No trades. No exceptions.

lines: Of the fourteen people in this office, I drew Toby. One in fourteen.
Somebody rigged this. Probably God. God hates me and loves Toby. For some reason.

scenes.recap: Jim tells the camera he drew Pam, and shows the box he's been filling for weeks.

beats.caption: slips a slip of paper reading PAM into his pocket

lines: I drew Pam. Which is a coincidence. A good one.
I've had her gift for three weeks. I didn't know I'd draw her. I was going to give it to her anyway. Don't tell her that.

beats.caption: peeks into a small shoebox wrapped in Sunday comics

beats.text: What's in the box?
Your Secret Santa gift. It's a live cricket.
I knew it.

scenes.recap: The Party Planning Committee splits over music: Angela wants a 'classic, quiet' party, Kelly and Phyllis want karaoke.

beats.text: Christmas karaoke. In the conference room. I already rented the machine.
The Christmas party will be classic. Cider. A wreath. Quiet reflection.
Angela, last year's party was so quiet Kevin fell asleep standing up.
Then have your karaoke. In the conference room. I'll be in the break room. With the people who matter.

lines: There are two Christmas parties now. That's like, double Christmas.
Mine has a disco ball. Angela's has a bowl of nuts.

scenes.recap: Michael tries to trade Toby with everyone, illegally; nobody will take him.

beats.text: Dwight. I'll trade you. My slip for your slip. Sight unseen. You'd be doing your country a service.
I can't. Mine is... very important. Medically important.
Kevin. Trade. I'll throw in twenty dollars.
Who'd I get?
I can't say. Rhymes with... no-bee.
No.
Don't even walk over here.

scenes.recap: Oscar works out that Dwight and Angela drew each other, which is very unlikely, and very interesting.

beats.text: Dwight, who did you draw? I won't tell.
Toby.
Michael drew Toby. He announced it. Twice.
Oscar, don't you have numbers to look at?

lines: The bobbleheads. The blanket. The way they both pretend to hate the other one exactly the same amount.
I'm not saying anything. I'm just keeping a file. Mentally. It's a thick file.

scenes.recap: Michael tries to reunite the two parties, runs between them, and ends up bringing the karaoke machine to the cider.

beats.text: THE PARTY (PARTIES)
Angela. Two parties is not Christmas. Christmas is about togetherness. And presents. Mostly togetherness.
Tell that to the karaoke traitors.
I like this party. Nobody's singing.
TWO MINUTES LATER
Compromise! Karaoke. But only quiet songs. Silent Night only.

beats.caption: sings Silent Night in a surprisingly lovely baritone

scenes.recap: Pam opens Jim's gift: a box of their inside jokes. Jim quietly pockets the card before she sees it.

beats.caption: opens a shoebox wrapped in Sunday comics

beats.text: A Twix. The beets game. A tiny umbrella from the Dundies?
Is this the cricket radio? And... a sketchbook. 'For the children's books.'

beats.caption: slides a folded card out of the box and into his pocket

beats.text: Jim. This is... how did you remember all this?
I have a good memory. For umbrellas.

lines: I saw that. I see things. I'm a vault, but I have eyes.

scenes.recap: Dwight and Angela exchange suspiciously perfect gifts in the kitchen.

beats.caption: gives her a tiny wooden cat, hand-carved

beats.text: It's Sprinkles. To scale. I used a photo.

beats.caption: gives him a pocketknife engraved D.K.S.

beats.text: For the farm. And for whittling. More cats.
Oh. Sorry. Am I interrupting the Secret Santa you two definitely didn't do?
Get out.

scenes.recap: Michael gives Toby a Monopoly 'Get Out of Jail Free' card; Toby, who drew Michael, gives him an engraved pen that says 'Regional Manager, Scranton.'

beats.caption: hands Toby a Monopoly 'Get Out of Jail Free' card

beats.text: Merry Christmas. Keep it on you. You never know.
Thanks. I actually drew you too. Here.

beats.caption: unwraps a heavy pen engraved: MICHAEL SCOTT, REGIONAL MANAGER, SCRANTON

beats.text: Whatever corporate decides, you should have something that says it.
This is a very nice pen, Toby. I still hate you.

lines: Toby got me the best gift I've ever gotten. Which is so typical of Toby.
He ruins everything. Even hating him.

scenes.recap: After the party, Pam asks if there was a card; Jim says no, and the card stays in his pocket.

beats.text: Best gift I've ever gotten. I mean it. Was there a card? There's usually a card.
No. No card. Just the umbrella.
Merry Christmas, Jim.

lines: What does the card say? It says... stuff. It said too much. It's for another time.
Or never. Never's also a time.

scenes.recap: After everyone leaves, Kelly sings karaoke alone to Ryan, who stays.

beats.caption: belts out a Christmas power ballad to an empty conference room

beats.text: Everyone's gone, Kelly.
You're not.
One more song.
